blogs.title: When DIC Isn’t the Whole Story: Spotting CM-HUS After Sepsis
blogs.description: How to recognize when persistent thrombocytopenia and new hemolysis emerging after early sepsis improvement signal a superimposed thrombotic microangiopathy. Practical triggers to reassess the diagnosis, key labs (LDH, haptoglobin, schistocytes), and avoiding anchoring on DIC.

blogs.title: The Dog-Bite Septic Shock You Can’t Miss: Capnocytophaga canimorsus in Healthy Adults
blogs.description: A fast review of Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis in immunocompetent hosts: clinical clues (hypoglycemia, leukopenia, DIC), mortality risk, culture delays, the role of molecular diagnostics, and evidence-based empiric/definitive antibiotics for severe dog/cat–associated infections.

blogs.title: MAHA in Real Time: A Practical Algorithm to Separate TTP, STEC-HUS, and CM-HUS
blogs.description: A bedside pathway for adults with MAHA + thrombocytopenia ± AKI: using PLASMIC, when to start PEX immediately, how ADAMTS13 results re-route management, ruling out STEC-HUS, and recognizing the CM-HUS phenotype that benefits from complement blockade.

blogs.title: Normal C3/C4, Sick Kidneys: Interpreting Complement Tests in Suspected CM-HUS
blogs.description: Why normal C3/C4 don’t exclude CM-HUS; how timing, PEX, and eculizumab alter complement assays; the role of AH50/CH50 and extended genetic testing; and how to counsel teams when labs seem discordant with the clinical picture.

blogs.title: Complement Blockade on a Tightrope: Starting Eculizumab After Bacteremia—Timing, Vaccines, and Prophylaxis
blogs.description: Navigating the risk-benefit of eculizumab in the setting of recent sepsis: when to initiate after cultures clear, meningococcal vaccination strategy (MenACWY, MenB), antibiotic prophylaxis if therapy can’t wait, and monitoring for invasive infections while treating CM-HUS.

blogs.title: The Misleading DAT: Penicillins, Transfusions, and the Hemolysis Red Herring
blogs.description: DAT-positive hemolysis that isn’t autoimmune: how drug exposure (e.g., penicillins) and recent transfusion can confound interpretation. Pearl: persistent schistocytosis and steroid-refractory hemolysis should refocus clinicians on TMA rather than warm AIHA.

blogs.title: Dog and Cat Bites in 2026: Empiric Coverage That Won’t Miss Capnocytophaga
blogs.description: Evidence-based empiric and step-down regimens for serious bite-related infections, acknowledging beta-lactamase–producing Capnocytophaga. Practical tips on initial IV choices, outpatient prophylaxis, allergy workarounds, and duration—plus what to send to the lab and how long to incubate.

blogs.title: Biopsy at 77k Platelets: How—and Why—to Pursue Renal Pathology in TMA
blogs.description: Decision-making around kidney biopsy in thrombocytopenic patients: risk mitigation, thresholds, and how histology (fibrin thrombi, ischemic glomeruli, ATN) sharpens the diagnosis and guides therapy in CM-HUS versus DIC-associated kidney injury.

blogs.title: Blue Toes, Warm Pulses: Recognizing Microthrombotic Ischemia in DIC and TMA
blogs.description: Clinical recognition of distal ischemic changes with preserved pulses as a microthrombotic phenomenon, how to differentiate from embolic or vasculitic processes, and what this sign should trigger in your diagnostic and management plan.
